app.name: CulitosTracker
app.tagline: Her cycle, your relationship, and how you're both doing. One place.

landing.intro: Track your partner's cycle with their consent, understand what phase they're in, keep the dates that matter and get suggestions based on how you're both doing.
landing.consent: Another person's data is stored only with their consent, and predictions are estimates: never a contraceptive method.

relationship.body: Anniversaries, milestones and time together, with advice that adapts to the stage you're in.

checkins.title: Check-ins from both
checkins.body: Each person logs how they feel. Nobody invents anybody's emotions.

ranking.body: An optional, anonymous leaderboard for those keeping count.

today.1: Today is your anniversary: {{years}} years with {{name}}. Don't let it pass without marking it, even with something small.
today.2: {{years}} years with {{name}} today. A message first thing already changes the day.
today.3: Anniversary: {{years}} years. Bring up a moment from the first year with {{name}}; it usually beats any gift.

upcoming.1: Your anniversary is in {{days}} days ({{years}} years). Good time to prepare something special.
upcoming.2: In {{days}} days you reach {{years}} years. If you want to book something, this week is the moment.
upcoming.3: {{days}} days until the anniversary. Think about what made {{name}} happy last year and repeat the idea, not the plan.

approaching.1: Your anniversary is coming up ({{days}} days). If you want to plan something ahead, now is the time.
approaching.2: {{days}} days to the anniversary. Jot down one idea today, even if you settle it later.
approaching.3: The anniversary with {{name}} is in {{days}} days. Without giving anything away, ask what kind of plan sounds good lately.

today.1: Today is {{name}}'s birthday: she turns {{age}}. Make yours the first message she gets.
today.2: {{name}} turns {{age}} today. You have {{wishes}} ideas saved on her list; if you didn't get there in time, an improvised plan counts too.
today.3: {{name}}'s birthday. Time before gifts: keep the evening free for her.

upcoming.1: In {{days}} days {{name}} turns {{age}}. Check her saved gift ideas ({{wishes}}) and decide now.
upcoming.2: {{days}} days to {{name}}'s birthday. If you're booking something, this is the week.
upcoming.3: {{name}}'s birthday is in {{days}} days. Without giving anything away, ask whether she'd rather have a quiet plan or a celebration.

approaching.1: {{name}}'s birthday is coming up ({{days}} days). Add one idea to her gift list today.
approaching.2: {{days}} days until {{name}} turns {{age}}. Notice what she mentions these weeks: that's the gift.
approaching.3: {{name}}'s birthday is in {{days}} days. If you want to organize something with more people, start letting them know.

sad.1: {{name}} said she isn't feeling great today. You can ask whether she wants to talk or would rather just have company.
sad.2: {{name}} logged a sad day. It doesn't need fixing: a short message and being available already helps.
sad.3: According to her check-in, {{name}} is having a sad day. Ask what would help this evening and do it without commentary.

low.1: {{name}} logged a hard day. Ask what she needs instead of assuming it.
low.2: {{name}} marked a heavy day. Take one task off her list that you can do yourself.
low.3: By her check-in, {{name}} is stressed or anxious. Skip the plans today: suggest something quiet or nothing at all.

good.1: {{name}} logged a good day. Ask what made it good and listen.
good.2: {{name}} is in good spirits according to her check-in. Good moment to bring up that pending plan.
good.3: {{name}} marked a good day. Tell her something good about yours and share the mood.

needsSpace.1: You noted she seems to need space. Ask her directly what she needs instead of assuming.
needsSpace.2: You noticed {{name}} needs space. One line, "I'm here", and don't push.
needsSpace.3: By what you logged, {{name}} wants distance. Make a plan of your own today and leave the door open.

sad.1: You noted she seems sad today. A simple message asking how she is can open the door without pressure.
sad.2: You noticed {{name}} seems sad. Instead of "what's wrong?", try "do you want company or some time alone?".
sad.3: You logged sadness in {{name}}. It's your perception: ask if you got it right before acting.

upset.1: You noted she seems upset. Listen first and understand what happened before defending yourself or fixing it.
upset.2: You noticed {{name}} seems upset. Ask whether it has to do with you; if the answer is no, don't push.
upset.3: By what you logged, {{name}} is upset. Avoid pending topics today and let the anger settle before talking.

distant.1: You noted she seems distant. Sometimes it's tiredness, sometimes something else: ask without drama.
distant.2: You noticed {{name}} seems distant. Suggest something small and low-pressure: a walk, a coffee.
distant.3: You logged distance in {{name}}. Before reading into it, ask how her day went.

happy.1: You noted {{name}} seems happy. Good day to propose that plan you keep postponing.
happy.2: You noticed {{name}} in good spirits. Ask what brightened her day; telling it makes it last longer.
happy.3: By what you logged, {{name}} is happy. It's the moment to talk about something pending, on the right foot.

affectionate.1: You noted {{name}} seems affectionate. Answer with time, not just words: a while together without phones.
affectionate.2: You noticed {{name}} affectionate today. Return the gesture with something concrete: a message, a plan, a note.
affectionate.3: By what you logged, {{name}} is affectionate. Good moment to suggest a date and put a date on it.

tired.1: You noted {{name}} seems tired. Better a short plan or none today, and you handle dinner.
tired.2: You noticed tiredness in {{name}}. Ask if she wants an earlier night, and join her.
tired.3: By what you logged, {{name}} is worn out. Take one task off her day without announcing it.

stressed.1: You noted {{name}} seems stressed. Ask what's on her plate and offer help with one concrete thing.
stressed.2: You noticed stress in {{name}}. Today isn't the day for long talks; it is for a practical gesture.
stressed.3: By what you logged, {{name}} is tense. Don't add plans, and ask what would take pressure off.

notSure.1: You noted you're not sure how {{name}} is. The fastest way to know is to ask straight out.
notSure.2: You're unsure how {{name}} seems. Try a concrete question: "how was your day, 1 to 10?".
notSure.3: You marked "not sure". Time together without an agenda usually clears it up faster than guessing.

stressed.1: You both seem to be having a heavy day. Maybe a quiet plan beats trying to solve everything today.
stressed.2: Stress on both sides. Leave any thorny topic for tomorrow and have a calm dinner.
stressed.3: You're both tense today. Split the evening chores and don't expect much from each other.

good.1: You both logged a good day. Propose that plan you keep postponing.
good.2: Good day for both of you. Go celebrate for no reason, even if it's just a drink nearby.
good.3: You're both doing well today. It's the moment to talk about a shared project, big or small.

quietPlan.1: You're tired and you notice stress in {{name}}. Maybe today calls for a quiet plan and talking without pressure.
quietPlan.2: You're low on energy and {{name}} is stressed. Simple dinner, sofa, and nothing to solve today.
quietPlan.3: Not the day for big plans: you're tired and {{name}} is tense. A short walk may be enough.

low.1: You logged that you're not okay today. Tell {{name}} in one sentence; she doesn't have to guess.
low.2: Your check-in marks a low day. Ask for what you need, even if it's just quiet company.
low.3: You're not okay today, by your own log. Take care of yourself first: one small thing for you before the relationship.

stressed.1: You logged high stress. Let {{name}} know so she doesn't read it as distance.
stressed.2: You're stressed. Before talking about anything important, give yourself a moment to slow down.
stressed.3: Your stress is high today. Make clear it isn't about the relationship, if that's the case.

tired.1: You logged low energy. Suggest a short plan or none; don't force it.
tired.2: You're running on empty today. Say so before it comes across as disinterest.
tired.3: Low energy by your check-in. Delegate dinner or ask for help with one thing.

lowSatisfaction.1: You logged low satisfaction with the relationship. Write down in two lines what you're missing before bringing it up.
lowSatisfaction.2: Your check-in marks dissatisfaction. Pick one concrete thing you'd like to change and propose it this week.
lowSatisfaction.3: Low satisfaction today. Ask yourself whether it's a bad day or a trend; if it's a trend, it's time to talk.

affectionate.1: You're feeling affectionate today. Say it or show it before the day slips by.
affectionate.2: You logged a lot of affection. A small physical gesture is worth more than keeping it in.
affectionate.3: You're in the mood for closeness. Suggest time together without screens tonight.

good.1: You logged a good day. Share the mood: tell {{name}} what went well.
good.2: You're doing well today. Do something for {{name}} you've been putting off.
good.3: Good day by your check-in. Propose a weekend plan while the energy is there.

menstruation.1: According to what's logged, {{name}} may be on her period. Everyone experiences it differently: ask what she feels like.
menstruation.2: The calendar estimates {{name}} is on her period. Keep what relieves her handy and ask before suggesting plans.
menstruation.3: By the estimate, {{name}} would be on her period. It's a calendar figure, not a mood: ask how she is.

lead.2: Relationships hold together through the small stuff of every day.
lead.3: An ordinary day is also an opportunity.
lead.6: Nobody guesses what the other person needs.
lead.7: The week's tiredness shows up in the relationship too.
lead.8: Routine isn't bad; not noticing it is.
lead.9: Caring for the relationship doesn't mean hovering.
lead.10: Important conversations rarely start on their own.
lead.11: It's easy to take for granted the person you see every day.
lead.12: Small things count more when nobody expects them.
lead.13: Each of you arrives at the day carrying your own weight.
lead.14: A good moment together almost always starts with a question.
lead.15: Listening is a form of affection too.
lead.16: Agreeing on everything isn't the goal.
lead.17: Early on, a lot gets assumed and little gets said.
lead.18: Over time, talking logistics replaces actually talking.
lead.19: A packed week leaves little room for a calm conversation.
lead.20: Misunderstandings grow fast when each of you is busy with your own thing.
lead.21: Some topics get postponed because they seem minor.
lead.23: Nobody gets tired of knowing they're seen.
lead.24: What you value in the other person doesn't always reach them.
lead.25: The first months are full of compliments; later they're taken as given.
lead.26: Recognizing an effort on time beats celebrating it late.
lead.27: The best plan isn't the most expensive one.
lead.28: Weeks fill themselves if nobody books a gap.
lead.29: Early on, every plan is a way of getting to know each other.
lead.30: After so many plans together, novelty has to be sought out.
lead.31: There are days for going out and days for staying in.
lead.32: Intimacy is cared for outside the bedroom too.
lead.33: What you feel like changes from day to day, and that's normal.
lead.34: With trust, it's easier to talk about what you like and what you don't.
lead.35: Early on, ask more and assume less.
lead.36: Desire doesn't always line up for both of you.
lead.37: Being together all the time proves nothing.
lead.38: Each of you needs time that is only yours.
lead.39: According to what's logged, these days may call for calm rather than activity.
lead.40: Having plans of your own takes nothing from the relationship.
lead.41: Time alone recharges the couple too.
lead.42: Arguing isn't the problem; arguing badly is.
lead.43: The first disagreements set how the next ones get resolved.
lead.44: Over the years, some arguments repeat with the same script.
lead.45: When one of you arrives tense, any comment weighs double.
lead.46: Being right and fixing things don't always go together.
lead.47: There's still a lot you don't know about this person.
lead.48: Over the years, it's easy to believe you already know everything about each other.
lead.49: Curiosity about the other person is practiced; it doesn't come on its own.
lead.50: Last year's answers may have changed.
lead.51: Knowing their routines says more than any big question.
lead.52: According to the calendar, these may be lower-energy days for {{name}}.
lead.53: A bad day doesn't always need a solution.
lead.54: Keeping company is different from fixing.
lead.55: Sometimes the support that works is the quietest kind.
lead.56: According to the calendar, {{name}} would be near ovulation. It's an estimate, not a certainty.

action.1: Ask how her week is going before telling her about yours.
action.2: Find ten screen-free minutes to talk about something that isn't logistics.
action.3: If there's something you've kept quiet for days, say it today in one short sentence.
action.4: Repeat in your own words what she tells you before answering; you'll see if you understood.
action.5: Tell her one thing that worries you, even if it seems small.
action.6: Ask what she needs instead of assuming.
action.7: Send a midday message with no reason and no question.
action.8: When she talks, put the phone face down.
action.9: Suggest a fixed slot this week to catch up calmly.
action.10: Ask what drained her energy today and listen without solving.
action.11: Say out loud one concrete thing she did this week that you liked.
action.12: Thank her for something everyday that usually passes without comment.
action.13: Recall a recent moment that made you smile and tell her about it.
action.14: Make her coffee, her tea or whatever she usually has, unasked.
action.15: Write a short note and leave it where she'll find it.
action.17: Notice an effort of hers nobody has acknowledged and name it.
action.18: Tell her what you admire about how she handled a hard situation.
action.19: When she gets home, pause what you're doing for a moment to say hello.
action.20: Remind her why you like spending time with her.
action.21: Propose a plan for this week and give it a day and a time.
action.22: Pick somewhere new for dinner, even if it's around the corner.
action.23: Plan a short walk with no set destination.
action.24: Cook something together that neither of you has made before.
action.25: Set aside an afternoon with no obligations and decide the plan as you go.
action.26: Suggest redoing your first date, same place or somewhere similar.
action.27: Find an event in your city for the weekend and ask if she's up for it.
action.28: A night in counts: a film, a blanket and no phones.
action.29: Let her choose the plan and don't argue the choice.
action.30: Go out for breakfast on a weekday.
action.31: Ask what she feels like today instead of assuming.
action.32: Talk about what you like as naturally as you'd talk about a film.
action.33: If you don't feel like something, say so without excuses; clarity is care too.
action.34: Spend a while on touch with no expectations: a long hug, a hand on the back.
action.35: Ask what she'd like to try, and listen without judging.
action.36: Remind her that a "no" from either of you needs no explanation.
action.37: Talk about what worked last time, not only what didn't.
action.38: Start the day with a small physical gesture before rushing out.
action.39: Suggest talking about intimacy at a calm moment, not in bed.
action.40: Ask whether there's anything she'd like to change and thank her for the answer, whatever it is.
action.41: Make a plan of your own today, without your partner, and tell her without justifying it.
action.42: Ask whether she'd rather have company or some time alone, and respect the answer.
action.43: Don't fill the silence; sometimes being close without talking is enough.
action.44: Encourage her to see her friends without having to ask permission.
action.45: Set aside half an hour for something only you enjoy.
action.46: If you notice she needs space, say it in one sentence and leave it there.
action.47: Go to bed when you need to, even if the other is still up.
action.48: Ask before proposing a plan: maybe today isn't the day.
action.49: Let a hard conversation wait today if neither of you has the energy.
action.50: Look after your own rest: sleeping well looks after the relationship too.
action.51: If there's an argument pending, suggest talking it through tomorrow calmly instead of today in a rush.
action.52: In the next argument, listen to the end before answering.
action.53: Apologize for your part, even if the other doesn't.
action.55: Agree on a signal to pause when an argument heats up.
action.56: Ask what she needs to feel heard, not who's right.
action.57: Clear up a recent misunderstanding instead of letting it slide.
action.58: Before replying to a comment that bothered you, count to ten.
action.59: Acknowledge out loud one point where the other was right.
action.60: If the argument keeps repeating, write in two lines what really bothers you.
action.61: Ask her a question you've never asked before.
action.62: Ask about her best childhood memory.
action.63: Ask what excites her right now, even if you think you know.
action.64: Take an interest in something of hers that you don't find interesting.
action.65: Ask what she'd do with a whole free day and no obligations.
action.66: Find out which song puts her in a good mood and play it.
action.67: Ask what she'd change about her routine if she could.
action.68: Ask about her day with a concrete question, not a "how was it?".
action.69: Ask what she learned this week.
action.70: Ask her to tell you something she's never told you.
action.71: Ask whether she wants to talk or would rather just have company.
action.72: Offer help with a specific task instead of a "let me know if you need anything".
action.73: Keep handy whatever usually relieves her on hard days.
action.74: Send a short message: "thinking of you", and nothing else.
action.75: Listen without offering solutions unless she asks for them.
action.76: Take care of dinner today without announcing it.
action.77: Ask what would help her tomorrow, not just today.
action.78: If she comes home late and drained, greet her with calm, not questions.
action.79: Note down what helped this time; it'll be useful next time.
action.80: Make clear that a bad day of hers isn't a problem for you.

closer.3: It doesn't have to come out perfect.
closer.6: And notice how the day changes.
closer.7: Better today than when it's due.
closer.9: If it goes wrong, there's another chance tomorrow.

how.title: How it's calculated
how.base: Each encounter is worth a base 10 XP.
how.age: Partner's age: +1 XP per year over 18 (max +40).
how.weight: Recorded weight: +1 XP per 2 kg over 50 (max +25).

how.loyalty: Loyalty: +5% per consecutive encounter with the same person, up to +50%.
how.note: The multipliers stack: farming XP with a single person in a serious relationship yields up to ×2.25 per encounter.

privacy.title: Privacy & consent
privacy.intro: CulitosTracker stores sensitive information: menstrual cycles, emotions and relationship data. These are the rules it runs on.

consent.title: Consent
consent.body: When you register a person manually you confirm you have their consent to store their data, including cycle data. If that person creates their own account and links it, they decide what is shared back and can revoke it at any time.

checkins.title: Check-ins
checkins.body: Your check-ins are yours. The other person only sees your mood if you explicitly share it, and notes are never shared.

observations.title: Observations
observations.body: What you record about how your partner seems is your perception and only you see it. The app never presents it as a fact about the other person.

estimates.title: Cycle estimates
estimates.body: Phases, ovulation and the fertile window are estimates computed from the recorded data. They are not medical information and don't work as contraception.

leaderboard.title: Ranking
leaderboard.body: You only appear if you opt in. Only your alias, your emoji if you want, and an aggregate number are published. Never partner names, dates or notes.

authorization.title: Server-side authorization
authorization.body: Every request validates on the server that the data belongs to you or was shared with you. Hiding things in the interface is never the only barrier.
